beats.text: Here is home, at I-and-J today. Look at the banner: no tasks scheduled. Today is a rest day — zero areas due. So it's the perfect day to show you how the schedule actually works.
Down in the nav, tap the Areas button — second from the left. Not the scan button in the middle; that one is for checking in on the day. Areas is where you see the plan.
Every area at the site, and what each one owes. The green tag says lyve, meaning right now — this really is today. And today, every area reads zero of zero due. Nothing is scheduled.
Open any area. No tasks due on Sunday. But say you are called in anyway — the work does not disappear, it simply is not on today's schedule.
So switch to Off-schedule. Here is everything this area can be checked on, even when it is not due. Record only what you actually did — nothing here is forced.
Now the part that makes planning easy. Up top is the schedule date. Slide it forward to any day, and see exactly what is coming.
Tomorrow — Monday. The tag flips to READ ONLY: this is a preview, it never records anything. And watch the numbers wake up. Site Operations: sixty-nine tasks due. A full working day.
Now jump to Friday. Same areas — but Site Operations climbs to seventy-two, and the canteen goes from nine to twelve. Those extra checks are the weekly and monthly tasks that land on a Friday.
Open Site Operations on that Friday: twenty-six checks due — twenty-three every shift, plus three periodic. You can see exactly what Friday holds, days before it arrives.
One rule to remember. A preview plans — it never ticks a box. Due and off-schedule, view only. To actually record the work, you scan the area, on the day.
